narrative.overview: The app edits what Google shows: titles, URLs and descriptions. So it looks like the page where those things live. A white sheet, a cool grey rail, one indigo for links and actions, URL green for paths. Wherever a page appears with its title or description, it is drawn as a search result. Everything else stays out of the way: hairlines instead of shadows, flat metric rows instead of decorated tiles, one tab style, one button shape.
keyCharacteristics: Left rail with every page visible at once, grouped Today / Fix / Create / Research / Setup
Page header in place of a top bar: group, title, one-line purpose, related pages, actions on the right
The search snippet as the signature component
Indigo means "you can act here"; green means a path or a good state; red and amber mean state only

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Indigo marks what you can act on. If it isn't a link, a primary action or the current selection, it is not indigo.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Red, amber and green appear only when they say something about a value. No decorative tints, no per-section accent colours.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels or tracked-out kickers anywhere. Labels read like words.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: A card at rest has a hairline, never a shadow.

dos: Do use the search snippet wherever a page's title or description is shown.
Do add every new page to `app/nav.py`; the rail, header, related links and ⌘K read it.
Do put a page's main action in the header with `data-page-action`.
Do link every number to the page where you act on it.
donts: Don't add uppercase labels, eyebrow text above titles, or per-section accent colours.
Don't use gradients, glows or coloured side stripes.
Don't give filter pills a solid fill; solid means action.
Don't add a per-page store picker; the rail owns the store.
